member_rule: single defined peptide; the IC50 is the peptide's own value against xanthine oxidase
xanthine substrate, uric-acid readout (absorbance 290-295 nm or HPLC); the readout is recorded, never an exclusion; many abstracts do not state it
one stated number (no range, inequality, single-concentration %, or figure reading)
uM/mM/mmol/L as read; mass units converted only for plain standard-residue linear peptides (ExPASy average residue masses + 18.015)
material recorded (synthetic/purified/unknown), not an exclusion; designed sequences allowed and flagged
the scored species' own peptides are never members
known_limits: Most members were read at abstract level: enzyme source and readout are often not stated.
Four whey dipeptides (GL, PM, AL, AM) were measured by HPLC; the others by absorbance where stated.
Values span 173 uM to 108 mM; several weak members come from AI or docking screens whose candidates were then synthesised and measured.

issues: Abstract-only verification: no OA full text (Europe PMC isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, no PMCID; Unpaywall is_oa=false), so assay conditions could not be read
XO enzyme source (e.g. bovine milk) not stated in the abstract
Substrate xanthine / uric-acid-formation readout not explicitly stated; abstract states only 'an improved HPLC method'
The other 12 di-/tri-peptides identified have no stated IC50 in the abstract, so only FH is verifiable from this source

Criterion 4 arithmetic recomputed: 25.7 mM x 1000 = 25700 uM, matches the listed ic50_uM exactly; no mass-unit conversion needed. MW sanity check only: F 147.1766 + H 137.1411 + 18.015 = 302.33, which matches the 302.33 Da given for FH in review PMC11719947.

Criterion 2 partially unverifiable: enzyme source (e.g. bovine milk XO) is not stated anywhere in the accessible text, so it could not be recorded. The abstract names only 'an improved HPLC method'; that the HPLC readout quantifies uric acid is standard for XO assays but is not spelled out in any text I could see (Unpaywall is_oa=false, Europe PMC isOpenAccess=N, no OA copy exists).

Criterion 6 flag (does not refute, but is the one thing that could move the value): review PMC11678060 (Nutrients 2024) Table 1 lists a second row 'FH IC50: 257.0 uM' under reference [79] = Yu et al. 2021, J Sci Food Agric 101:1349-1354, doi 10.1002/jsfa.10745, PMID 32820534. That paper's own abstract reports only EEAK at 173.00 +/- 0.06 uM and never mentions FH; it is paywalled (Unpaywall is_oa=false) so I could not read its full text. Review PMC10742721, which also summarises Yu 2021, reports only EEAK percent-inhibition figures and no FH. 257.0 uM is exactly 100x below 25.70 mM, consistent with a mM->uM garble in that one table. If the 257 uM value is genuine, criterion 6 would make this member median(257, 25700) = 12978.5 uM instead of 25700 uM.

Duplicate check against the existing cohort (tmp/fill-4.3/croaker-xo-cohort/cohort_uM.json, 36 sequences): FH is absent, so no in-cohort duplicate. Note the cohort's GL 10200, PM 23820, AL 34490, AM 40450 and YNITGW 9780 are listed next to FH in secondary tables but are different sequences, so no collision.
Value independently corroborated as 25.7 / 25.70 mM by three OA reviews citing He 2019: PMC12006031, PMC11678060, PMC11719947, plus PMC10742721.
He 2019 reports 13 di-/tri-peptides but only FH's IC50 appears in the abstract; the other 12 values remain unverifiable at this access level (closed access, no OA location).
